valuation.vl3_basis: trailing P/E, 5 years (price / last-12-month SEC diluted EPS), labelled

dm4.name: Vehicle deliveries growth
dm4.source: Tesla quarterly production and deliveries release (on release, ~2nd day of each quarter)
dm4.what: How many cars Tesla handed to customers in the latest quarter vs the same quarter last year (Tesla's delivery release).
dm4.why: Cars are about three quarters of Tesla's revenue, and this number arrives two to three weeks before the results.
dm4.bull_means: More cars delivered than a year ago: car demand is growing.
dm4.neutral_means: Deliveries roughly flat vs a year ago.
dm4.bear_means: Fewer cars delivered than a year ago: car demand is shrinking.

dm4.name: Energy storage deployed growth
dm4.source: Tesla quarterly production and deliveries release (GWh deployed)
dm4.what: How much battery storage (GWh, Megapack and Powerwall) Tesla installed in the latest quarter vs the same quarter last year.
dm4.why: Storage is the fastest-growing and most profitable hardware business (energy gross margin 29% vs 19% for automotive, last 4 quarters); it has grown 40-100% a year since 2023, so +20% already means a slowdown.
dm4.neutral_means: Storage growth has slowed to under 20% a year.
dm4.bear_means: Storage installations have stopped growing or are shrinking.

dm5.name: Tesla China retail sales, last 3 months
dm5.source: China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) monthly retail figures for Tesla, via CnEVPost / CarNewsChina
dm5.measured_against: the same 3 months a year earlier
dm5.what: Cars Tesla sold to buyers in China over the last 3 months vs the same 3 months a year earlier (retail, so exports are left out).
dm5.why: China is Tesla's second-biggest market and its most competitive; this independent monthly figure shows demand from actual buyers before Tesla's quarterly numbers, without counting exports already in deliveries.
dm5.bull_means: Chinese buyers are buying more Teslas than a year ago.
dm5.neutral_means: China sales roughly flat vs a year ago.
dm5.bear_means: Chinese buyers are buying fewer Teslas than a year ago.

mix._note: Revenue mix (plan v0.4, not scored). Parts are Tesla's own revenue lines; profit is reported for two segments only: Automotive (cars, credits, leasing, services and other) and Energy generation and storage.
mix.note: Gross margin by Tesla's own cost lines: car sales and regulatory credits share one cost line (credits have almost no cost), leasing, services and other, and energy each have their own. Margins 3 years ago are blank for car sales, leasing and the company: Tesla's filings before Q3 2022 do not tag these costs, so Q4 2022 cannot be derived (by difference: automotive about 23.4%, company about 21.5%).
